claim:
For every real \(\lambda>\sqrt2\), let \(R_\lambda^2=(\mathbb R^2,N_\lambda)\) be the Banaś--Frączek plane
\[
N_\lambda(x_1,x_2)=\max\left\{\lambda|x_1|,\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(R_\lambda^2)=2\sqrt{1-\lambda^{-2}}.
\]
Writing \(t_\lambda=\sqrt{\lambda^2-1}\), the triple
\[
x=(1,t_\lambda),\qquad y=(1,-t_\lambda),\qquad z=(2,0)
\]
attains this Ptolemy ratio exactly.
integrity: The proof is self-contained: a global Hilbert comparison treats every active-branch combination, and an explicit exact triple supplies the matching lower bound. No numerical experiment or inaccessible source is used for correctness.
scientific_limitations: The new claim covers only lambda>sqrt(2) for the real two-dimensional Banaś--Frączek plane. It does not extend the result to the generalized p-family. The 2015 comparison article remains an access-limited bibliographic risk because a verified full text was not obtained.
title: Exact Ptolemy constant on the second Banaś--Frączek regime
